title: Local pipe and protocol 1
summary: A local-only named pipe the game opens when the bridge is enabled, with a per-session token, a user-only access list, newline-delimited JSON and an allowlist of methods, so host tools can talk to the running game.

rows.note: First in-game run of the pipe and the script-call context.

limits: Requests are capped at 64 KiB and 32 levels of nesting.
A rate limit covers every request (20 a second, bursts of 40 by default); the tools pace themselves at 18 a second in bursts of 36 and retry a rate_limited refusal for up to 4 s.
A connection that sends five malformed or unauthenticated requests is dropped; a client silent for 120 s is disconnected.
quirks: The security boundary is the Windows user at medium integrity: any process running as the same user can read the token and connect.
Clients open the pipe at the Identification impersonation level and check the server's PID against session.json before sending the token.

title: Game and script calls from native code
summary: Every game or script function is called the way script code calls it, with a caller frame and a context that is never null, on the game thread, so native reads and writes don't crash the game.

rows.note: The call that crashed before the fix returned with tweak_marker 1.

limits: Engine addresses the call needs are resolved at load; if the address library lacks one, every game method is refused for the session (script_calls_unavailable).

unknowns.question: Is the script_calls_unavailable refusal path right when an engine address is really missing?
unknowns.settle_by: Only a game build whose address library lacks an address can show it; knowledge/runtime-access.md lists it as built, not confirmed.

title: Script-layer gate across loads
summary: The bridge makes no script call between the scripts detaching for a load and the next session's player attaching; while the gate is closed game.status answers loading from the plugin and other game calls are refused game_loading.
quirks: Calls after a new attach but before the player attaches are never made; whether they would be safe is untested.
notes: Built after session 5's crash, when game.wait polled game.status just after game.load detached the scripts. Session 6 passed its load checks.

title: One writer and read-only observers
summary: One exclusive writer connection plus a bounded pool of independent read-only connections, so a watcher or catch-up reader can follow the game while another tool drives it.

rows.note: In practice: a read-only catch-up client ran beside the MCP writer all session with no bridge_busy and no effect on the writer; the row was not run as written.

limits: 0 to 8 read-only connections (3 by default); a second writer gets bridge_busy.
npc.pick, starting the recorder, game.saves, game.options.read and test.events with stims stay writer-only (read_only_connection).
Half the shared rate bucket's burst is reserved for the writer; readers can't fill the last slot of the 16-slot game-thread queue.
quirks: Recorder, supervisor and input leases follow the writer: an MCP connection holding them keeps the writer seat, so a CLI writer gets bridge_busy (Borg 4).
Scheduling bounds are established offline, not measured game latency.

title: One command catalogue
summary: Every command is defined once (name, plain text, input schema, permission class, undo note, refusals) and appears in the MCP server, the CLI and the session runner alike; errors are plain sentences with one next step.

rows.note: cc.apply refused in photo mode in plain words, nothing changed.

quirks: Permission classes are data, ready for a consent screen; the game-side gate is separate and final.
Write and control commands are appended to logs/commands-<day>.jsonl (ignored) with their input and undo note.

title: Undo on every write
summary: Each write logs what it changed with its reversal and returns a machine-readable undo the caller can send back to put the game as it was.

rows.note: world.time.set's undo restored the clock to the exact second.
DM undos after the debug-id validation fix.

quirks: A vehicle door's lock can't be read back, so a lock change keeps its save hold until a save loads (RB-225).

known_issues.summary: Undos returned by the DM toolkit named spawned things by a dynamic id that the same commands' input validation refused, so they could not be replayed (Borg 1, DV2). Fixed in 0.8.14 (debug-id undo validation), unverified.
